headline: Sesterce, a French AI infrastructure group, plans a Finnish data centre site costing more than €10 billion.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a company plan with a stated capacity; the figures come from the company's statement as reported by Reuters.
importance_line: It matters to Finland's power grid and to Jamsa, where the site would sit on a closed paper mill, but it is the company's own plan, the anchor customer is not named, and the 1 gigawatt goal is tied to market demand.
summary: Reuters reports that Sesterce, a French AI infrastructure group, plans a data centre site in Finland costing more than €10 billion ($11.21 billion), with a first 200 megawatt phase whose works are planned to start in 2026. The company says it already has an anchor customer and aims for more than 1 gigawatt of AI capacity in Finland over the longer term, in line with market demand.
notes: Source Reuters. Text read on Yahoo Finance, a copy of the Reuters wire; the Reuters link (found by search) is blocked here (HTTP 401), so it is given as the original link. Note paragraph (Full Report 5.3) applies because the original was not opened. Score 6 kept. The pool headline's $11 billion matches the report's $11.21 billion conversion.
